articles.title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?
articles.summary: The home secretary sets out plans to change requirements for permanent settlement in the UK.
articles.body:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has set out plans to overhaul immigration rules.

Proposals to change the requirements to qualify for permanent settlement in the UK were first outlined in detail in November 2025, when Mahmood was home secretary in Sir Keir Starmer's government.

Following a consultation , Mahmood has now announced her final decision on what changes should be taken forward.

Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers

What is settlement and indefinite leave to remain?

Indefinite leave to remain (ILR) – also known as settlement – gives someone the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like.

Under the current system, people with ILR can also apply for benefits if they are eligible.

People who have lived in the UK for 12 months after being given ILR can apply for British citizenship, if they also meet other requirements .

Under the government's plans, the standard length of time migrants will have to live in the UK to qualify for permanent settlement will double from five to 10 years.

Under this 10-year pathway, applicants must have earned at least £12,571 for five of the seven years immediately before being granted settlement.

However, there will be a shorter qualifying period of five years for certain groups, including:

People who earned at least £50,271 for three of five years immediately before applying for settlement

Care workers who earned at least £25,000 a year while meeting their visa conditions and arrived in the UK before May 2025

"Skilled" public service workers, such as doctors, nurses and teachers

Other health and education public service workers who fall below this skill level, for example nursing auxiliaries and teaching assistants, if they arrived in the UK before May 2025

People from Hong Kong who hold British National (Overseas) status

People earning over £125,141 a year, as well as "highly skilled" migrants such as those on Global Talent or Innovator Founder visas, will qualify after three years.

Migrants who have claimed certain benefits or breached immigration rules will only be able to settle after at least 20 years.

To qualify for settlement, migrants will also have to meet other conditions including:

Earn at least £12,571 a year for at least three years, aligned with the threshold for paying income tax

There will be a different set of rules for refugees – people who have been granted asylum in the UK because they are unable to return to their own country as they fear persecution.

Refugees who arrived in the UK through an official government scheme will qualify for settlement after five years.

However, other refugees will need to wait 10 years and either work or study.

Those who do not work or study will need to wait 20 years.

Refugees who arrived in the UK by small boat or another illegal route will have to wait 20 years if they work or study, and 30 years if they don't.

Will migrants already in the UK be affected?

The changes will apply to migrants who are already in the UK but not those who have already been granted settlement.

A partner who arrives with someone who then applies for ILR will be able to settle at the same time, as long as they meet the relevant requirements.

However, a partner who joins later will need to complete the same qualifying residence period before they are eligible for settlement.

Eligible couples will be able to combine their earnings to meet the minimum income requirement.

The household income threshold will be £25,142 – twice the individual minimum income requirement.

Children under 18 will continue to be able to settle with their parents.

They will be exempt from the income, government debt, English language and Life in the UK test requirements, but will remain subject to the relevant suitability and criminality requirements.

Young adults aged 18 to 24, who remain dependant on their family, will also continue to be able to settle alongside them.

They will be expected to meet all the adult mandatory requirements but not the individual income requirement.

Someone who is aged 25 or over when their family becomes eligible for settlement will be expected to qualify independently.

Eligible partners, parents and children of British citizens will continue to qualify for settlement after five years.

articles.title: Democrat Haley Stevens grilled on 11th-hour endorsement of Mike Rogers in tense interview
articles.summary: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens faced a grilling from Anderson Cooper over her last-minute endorsement of Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race.
articles.body: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens faced hard questions from her liberal interviewer about her last-minute decision to endorse Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan's Senate race on Sunday. "Your fellow Michigan congresswoman, Debbie Dingell, said that she talked to you at midnight last night and that you told her you were not going to endorse Mike Rogers. If that is true, what changed between then and this morning?" CNN host Anderson Cooper asked. Stevens responded, "This is just a weight off my shoulders, OK? Abdul has been getting angrier and angrier. I was trying to help, and I endorsed him. That [Rebellion PAC] ad was very painful. There are so many Democrats who want to vote for our Democratic nominee. And they’re just being told, ‘Hey, this a party you don’t belong in, or this is a campaign you don’t belong in.’ And I’ve never cast a present vote in the Congress. I'm making a decision here, and you know, that’s just where I landed on this. I woke up this morning… clear-eyed, fresh and focused on what was in my heart and that’s that." FORMER RIVAL DODGES FULL-THROATED EL-SAYED ENDORSEMENT AFTER BITTER SENATE PRIMARY Stevens announced her endorsement of Rogers on Sunday in a stunning about-face, following El-Sayed saying, in her words, she was "no longer welcome in his campaign." El-Sayed edged Stevens in their hotly contested Democratic primary race for the Senate nomination. The endorsement followed a controversial ad put up by Rebellion PAC, founded by The Young Turks host Cenk Uygur, in support of El-Sayed's campaign, which Stevens called antisemitic. She demanded El-Sayed condemn the ad and his campaign said it was not affiliated with the ad. El-Sayed said he disagreed with its contents, which showed grocery shoppers blaming Israel for rising prices. Cooper continued questioning Stevens about what prompted her change of heart. HALEY STEVENS RIPPED BY FELLOW DEMS FOR REFUSING TO EXPLICITLY BACK EL-SAYED: 'STAY THE F--- OFF TELEVISION' "I had some time to, you know, think. I wasn’t on the phone, I think, that late, but I know Debbie’s always working around the clock," Stevens said. "It might not have been midnight when I spoke with her. But I was there, and just alone with my thoughts. I was writing things out. And look, this level of anger, and the things that we are seeing, look, we all want Democrats to win. I’m a really proud Democrat. And by the way, Abdul’s got every other Democrat with him. He just doesn’t have me and a few other people who love this party. Nothing with me changed, Anderson." Cooper asked about an August social media post in which Stevens criticized Rogers, writing, "Mike Rogers will be another rubber stamp for Donald Trump’s dangerous agenda, we can’t afford to give MAGA another Senate seat in November." Asked why she was now supporting Rogers, Stevens pointed to El-Sayed and criticized what she described as his "anger" and "lack of kindness." At one point in the interview, Stevens said that it sounded like Cooper was angry with her as well, as he argued she wasn't answering his questions. "It sounds like last night was a really big night where a lot built up what the turning point was," Cooper said. HALEY STEVENS' FIANCE HAMMERS EL-SAYED, SAYS HE'LL VOTE FOR ROGERS "That’s your assumption, Anderson," Stevens said. "I mean, that’s your editorializing. I certainly didn’t say that." "But you were willing to be at a campaign event for him [El-Sayed]," Cooper said. "You wanted to be at a public event with him up until some point, I guess, yesterday. And it’s just an interesting change. And I think a lot of people are curious to try to understand it." Stevens paused for several seconds before asking, "Was that a question, Anderson, or –" "No, I wanted to see if you wanted to fill in silence, but you don't," Cooper said. Stevens paused again before saying Michiganders were going to the ballot box, and she had made her "proclamation clear." HASAN PIKER BRUSHES OFF DEMS WHO SEE HIM AS A LIABILITY, NAMES HIS '28 CHOICE Adrian Hemond, the CEO of Michigan-based consulting firm Grassroots Midwest, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "This endorsement would have had far more impact if she had done it a month ago. More than 2 million people have already voted." Stevens' office did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment. The Rogers campaign also did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Zeteo founder and former MSNBC host Mehdi Hasan called Stevens a "train wreck" in the interview. Republican CNN contributor Shermichael Singleton said he felt sorry for Stevens in response to the interview. Dingell, who came on CNN to speak with Cooper after Stevens, called it one of the "most painful" interviews she has ever watched. HALEY STEVENS URGES EL-SAYED TO DITCH HASAN PIKER AFFILIATION AFTER MICHIGAN PRIMARY "I’m not sure I would have done this if I’d known she was going to be on immediately before me," Dingell said. "I have been worried about her all last week. She’s a human being. I’ve had multiple conversations with her. I’m far from being the only one that has. And I’m very concerned that this has all become a distraction." Dingell claimed Stevens had told her she was not going to endorse Rogers. articles.title: Russian bombing of Ukrainian aid centre kills 26 people
articles.summary: Ukraine’s president calls attack further proof that Russia does not want any ‌kind of de-escalation or real justice.
articles.body:
A Russian ⁠bomb attack on an aid centre in Ukraine has killed 26 people, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, two more than were reported earlier by Ukraine’s emergency services.

The strikes destroyed a school used as a humanitarian aid distribution centre in the village of Komyshuvakha in the southeastern region of Zaporizhia, Zelenskyy said on Monday. Five other people are reported to have been injured.

“After the first air strike, there was a repeat strike with nine more bombs, ⁠directly on the shelter ⁠where people were gathered,” Ukraine’s president wrote on Telegram.

“The Russians could not have been unaware that ⁠every week residents who have remained in ⁠Komyshuvakha were receiving assistance ⁠aid right there. This is yet further proof that Russia does not want any ‌kind of de-escalation, any real justice.”

Footage posted by Ukrainian emergency services showed a building reduced to piles of smouldering rubble. Rescuers were shown working at the site.

Among those killed were a police officer and two State Emergency Service rescuers, regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin reported on Telegram.

Efforts to rescue people on Monday evening were hindered as Russian drones launched additional attacks in the area that had been bombed, according to Mykhailo Semikin, a military official in Zaporizhia.

“After the humanitarian operation in Oleshky , there was a moment when the next steps could have shown that progress toward peace was possible,” Zelenskyy said on social media. “With these killings, Russia is sending an entirely opposite signal: Russia is counting on more killings.”

Elsewhere in Ukraine, emergency services reported that drone strikes injured 12 people in the eastern Kharkiv region and damaged a refrigeration facility, greenhouses and residential buildings.

Five people were also reported injured in the Black Sea port city of Odesa, where a warehouse was targeted and homes were damaged.

Russia’s Ministry of Defence said that it shot down 212 Ukrainian drones overnight, while the head of Russia’s Samara region, Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, reported local air defences had repelled an aerial attack, without giving further details.

articles.title: If hackers can take control of a supermarket freezer, how vulnerable is other tech?
articles.summary: Dozens of shops across European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their fridges.
articles.body:
Supermarkets across Europe have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their fridges and freezers, and raising concern about the vulnerabilities of internet-connected hardware from industrial machinery to humble domestic appliances.

Smart devices which are connected to the internet can include fridges, central heating, and even washing machines.

And while that makes them easier to control remotely, in theory, any device which goes online can potentially be exploited by malicious actors.

However, that doesn't mean hackers can easily take control of it, and big brands generally go to great lengths to make sure their tech is secure.

Exploits have been found before in some devices. In 2015, researchers demonstrated how a vulnerability in a Samsung smart fridge could allow them to intercept internet traffic.

But there's no evidence domestic appliances are being targeted in the cyber-attacks which targeted supermarkets in November.

Ciaran Martin, former chief executive of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) says manufacturers needed to do more to make connected devices secure.

"There's a lot more that we need to demand of big tech to give us safer devices and products in the first place," he said.

He advised consumers to keep devices updated and enable multi-factor authentication wherever possible.

"I know it's a pain, but it only takes a few seconds," he said.

Since April 2024, UK law has required manufacturers of certain consumer smart devices to meet minimum cyber security standards, including requirements around passwords and security updates.

The NCSC said it was working with international partners and industry to understand the supermarket incidents, but it was unaware of any impact on the UK.

However, researchers from UK Cyber Defence have identified more than 800 refrigeration and building-control interfaces associated with British retailers that can be accessed over the public internet.

That doesn't necessarily mean they can be hacked, but it could leave them exposed to attackers exploiting weak passwords or software vulnerabilities.

The government has already held talks with senior food retailers about cyber resilience, following earlier attacks on supermarkets.

Helen Dickinson, chief executive of the British Retail Consortium, has said cyber incidents are a major concern for retailers, with businesses working alongside the NCSC to share intelligence and strengthen their defences.

It would not be the first time that hacks have raised concern about impact on food supply.

When UK supermarkets M&S and the Co-op were targeted by ransomware hackers in May 2025, the retailers struggled to stock some shop shelves with fresh deliveries.

Customers across the UK complained of empty shelves in the days following the attack.

Tom Hegel, a researcher at cyber-security firm SentinelOne, said retailers must be clearer about responsibility.

"The question retailers need to answer is who owns the security of that equipment, not just who repairs it," he said.

He said internet connectivity can make everyday technology more convenient, but security needed to keep pace.

"Once an attacker can operate those controls, legitimate functions such as defrosting become tools for disruption," he said.

"Changing a setting can destroy physical stock, not just interrupt a computer system."

Could cars, power plants and water supplies be vulnerable?

Outside of the home, connected tech is used to remotely manage industrial machinery and vehicles.

Cyber security expert Ken Munro pointed to a 2015 demonstration in which researchers remotely hacked a Jeep through its internet-connected entertainment system, prompting improvements in vehicle security.

"Fortunately, the vehicle industry woke up to this and fixed the problem," he said.

Mobile connections are also widely used to monitor equipment in power plants and water networks, allowing engineers to manage systems remotely.

Munro said UK utilities were generally good at securing these connections, but standards varied around the world.

His biggest concern was smaller, poorly funded utility companies which may still be relying on older, vulnerable equipment.

Without proper protections, "any factory or equipment" connected to the internet - ranging from carmakers to electricity or transport infrastructure - could face similar risks, said Olivier Daloy, a cybersecurity expert at Zscaler.

articles.title: Chili’s customers in North Carolina suffer burns after sipping margaritas mistakenly made with cleaning chemical
articles.summary: A Chili’s Grill & Bar in North Carolina is back in business after three customers and two workers suffered chemical burns on their mouths from sipping margaritas mistakenly made with a cleaning chemical last week.
articles.body: A Chili’s Grill & Bar in North Carolina is back in business after three customers and two workers suffered chemical burns on their mouths from sipping margaritas mistakenly made with a cleaning chemical last week. The eatery in Forest City was shut down on Thursday after the customers, who had ordered the drinks shortly after the restaurant opened for lunch, “immediately experienced discomfort and chemical burns in and around their mouths,” the Foothills Health District said in a statement. “Two restaurant employees subsequently tasted the substance and reported similar symptoms,” the FHD statement. It was reopened the next day after local health inspectors discovered that a worker “preparing the bar for lunch service discovered the unlabeled container and, believing its contents to be sugar, used the chemical to prepare the margarita station.” Chili’s, according to its menu, offers several margaritas that are make with a “citrus-sugar rimmer” in addition to the traditional salt. FHD spokesperson Megan Rollins said in an email the investigation was closed and no fines were issued. She said the injured parties received medical treatment, but had no information about their conditions. A Chili’s spokesperson said in an email that this was an “incident isolated to a single restaurant in Forest City, North Carolina, that resulted in injuries to two of our guests and Team Members.” “Our team took immediate action to support those affected and avoid further injuries,” the spokesperson said. “We have thoroughly investigated the circumstances and addressed the issues specific to this location.” The spokesperson did not respond to a follow-up question from NBC News seeking an explanation for why their tally of injured customers was different from the one provided earlier by the FHD. This Chili’s is located about 60 miles west of Charlotte, North Carolina. On the morning of Oct. 26, according to the FHD statement, “a restaurant employee received a granulated degreasing chemical from a contracted worker who was power washing the exterior, and placed it into an unlabeled container.” For reasons unclear, “the container was brought inside the restaurant and left in the bar area.” Two days later, those chemicals were inadvertently added to margaritas.

articles.title: Florida man preparing to sell his $500,000 home discovers $10 quitclaim deed affecting his ownership stake; ex-wife faces felony charge; former couple bought property for $265,000 in 2006
articles.summary: A Florida man preparing to sell his house, which he estimated was worth approximately $500,000, made an unexpected discovery when he learned that a
articles.body: A Florida man preparing to sell his house, which he estimated was worth approximately $500,000, made an unexpected discovery when he learned that a quitclaim deed listing just $10 in consideration had been recorded against the property. The document allegedly affected his ownership interest, despite his claim that he had never signed it or authorised anyone to transfer his share.His former wife, Sharon Joy Barnett, 56, of Margate, is now facing a first-degree felony charge involving the alleged fraudulent use of personal identification information.According to a Margate Police Department probable-cause affidavit, the disputed deed was recorded in March 2024. Investigators allege that Barnett used her former husband's identifying information without his consent in connection with the document.The $10 mentioned in the deed was its stated consideration and not the actual market value or confirmed sale price of the house.Florida man discovers disputed deed while preparing to sell homeThe former couple purchased the Margate residence in October 2006 for approximately $265,000, according to the police affidavit. They lived there for around 11 years before filing for divorce in July 2017.During the divorce proceedings, the husband moved out of the property. Their agreement reportedly stated that the house would be sold after their daughter turned 18, with the proceeds divided between them.However, when the man later contacted a real estate agent about listing the property, he discovered that a quitclaim deed affecting his ownership interest had been recorded in March 2024.In his statement to police, he said he had neither signed the document nor authorised anyone to sign it on his behalf or transfer his ownership interest.He estimated the house's current market value at approximately $500,000 and told investigators that the disputed filing had prevented him from proceeding with the sale.Notary's account reportedly changed during investigationDetectives also questioned the notary whose details appeared on the disputed quitclaim deed.According to the affidavit, the notary initially recalled notarising the document and told investigators that she had known Barnett personally for several years.However, during further questioning, she reportedly said she could not independently remember whether the former husband had been present when the document was purportedly signed.The affidavit also states that the notary did not have a journal or other contemporaneous record establishing the circumstances of the signing. Detectives noted that her accounts changed during a recorded interview conducted using body-camera footage.The circumstances surrounding the alleged signing are part of the investigation into the disputed property document.Sharon Joy Barnett faces first-degree felony chargeThe Broward County State Attorney's Office filed one count of criminal use of personal identification information against Barnett on October 6, 2026.The criminal information, filed in case 26-011939-CF10A, alleges that she fraudulently used another person's identifying information without consent between March 2 and October 14, 2024.The charge invokes Florida Statute 817.568(2)(c), which covers the alleged fraudulent use of personal identification information involving a financial value of at least $100,000.Prosecutors allege that the relevant benefit, avoided payment, injury or fraud met that threshold. The charge is classified as a first-degree felony.Traffic stop leads to Barnett's arrestBarnett was arrested on October 26, 2026, after a Margate police officer stopped her vehicle and discovered an outstanding warrant connected to the identity-fraud case.A Broward County magistrate found probable cause the following day, and a $5,000 surety appearance bond was filed.The allegations have not been proven in court. Barnett is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.Broward County offers property-owner alert serviceThe case also highlights the importance of monitoring property records. The Broward County Property Appraiser offers a free Owner Alert service that notifies registered users when its office processes a recorded document changing a property's ownership.The service provides owners with a link to the document, allowing them to review changes and identify transactions they may not have authorised.The property appraiser advises anyone who suspects deed fraud to notify local law enforcement and seek legal advice. Its office cannot determine which competing ownership claim is legally valid, a matter that may ultimately require a court ruling.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: German unions launch wave of strikes over cost-of-living pressures
articles.summary: The expanded industrial action comes amid a wave of strikes and protests that have sparked unrest across Europe.
articles.body:
Germany’s largest union has launched a wave of strikes as it pushes for higher wages and increased job security.

The walkouts on Monday escalated a wage dispute affecting about 3.7 million employees in Germany’s metal and electrical engineering industries. The expanded industrial action comes amid myriad strikes and protests across Europe over the cost of living and conditions in workplaces and educational facilities, several of which have seen severe unrest.

Major manufacturers including Audi, Mercedes-Benz and Tata Steel were affected by the strikes launched by the IG Metall union. The union is calling for a 5 percent pay rise amid cost-of-living pressures, as well as measures to protect jobs and production sites, and profit-sharing arrangements in sectors performing strongly.

Employers have proposed a one-off payment equivalent to 1 percent of pay in July 2027, followed by a 1.3 percent wage increase from July 2028. The proposal would allow companies facing financial difficulties to withhold the one-off payment.

IG Metall rejected the offer, saying it would amount to a pay cut in real terms, and called for the expansion of the industrial action.

Strikes are expected to continue throughout the week. The union plans to release participation figures on Friday. During the previous bargaining round in 2024, more than 100,000 workers took part on peak days.

The cost of living, housing costs, and education policy have provoked demonstrations across Europe in recent weeks. Students and unions have led mass rallies, and unrest has rocked Belgium, France and Spain among other countries.

The wave of protest reached Germany over the weekend, with thousands of people rallying in Berlin and more than 30 other German cities on Saturday.

articles.title: Trump signals progress on Iran deal as Tehran pushes faster ceasefire
articles.summary: Iran says its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz can be implemented in two days if the US agrees to terms.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has signalled progress towards a possible agreement with Iran, as Tehran pushes to accelerate its ceasefire proposal.

“It looks like that’s coming together very nicely,” Trump said on Monday at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, DC. “That’s why I guess the oil prices dropped. People found out about it.”

His comments followed a post on Truth Social in which he said Iran wanted a settlement “as soon as possible”, adding: “It could happen!”

Trump also claimed oil prices had fallen by almost $10 a barrel, attributing the decline to expectations that the war on Iran would end soon.

US Vice President JD Vance said Washington had held “a number of good conversations with the Iranians” and that he and Trump felt optimistic about the prospects for a negotiated settlement.

“We’re going to keep on working at it,” Vance told reporters at Joint Base Andrews.

“We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” he added.

Asked whether Washington had given Tehran a deadline to reach a deal before Trump resumed strikes, Vance said, “No, we haven’t set deadlines.”

He said Trump retained military and nonmilitary options, and that any agreement required “a firm commitment and a verifiable commitment” that Iran would not rebuild its nuclear programme, which Vance claimed the US had destroyed.

The US remarks came as Iranian officials said their seven-step plan remained unchanged but could now be implemented within two days rather than a week. The proposal includes a swift reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and a return to talks over Iran’s nuclear programme.

Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the offer had been “condensed and can be implemented within two days”.

“If Iran’s demands are met, it is possible that both security will be restored to the Strait of Hormuz and the negotiation process will begin within a short period of time,” Baghaei said. “All of this depends on how the American side wants to proceed regarding the future of this process.”

Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had granted “powers” to the government to accelerate talks with Washington to end the war, the state IRNA news agency reported.

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abbas Araghchi reiterated that Tehran was prepared for both diplomacy and military confrontation, as Qatar and Pakistan continued to facilitate indirect talks.

“By accepting these conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will be opened, and negotiations will resume,” Araghchi told IRNA in Ashgabat, Turkmenistan. “Otherwise, the current situation will continue, and Iran will not bow down.”

Iran previously said its plan could be implemented within a week if Washington met Tehran’s conditions. They include the US lifting its naval blockade of Iran’s ports, repealing sanctions, guaranteeing an end to strikes, and securing a complete regional ceasefire, especially in Lebanon.

Baghaei gave no indication that Tehran had changed its demands or that Washington had accepted its proposal.

Despite the latest expressions of optimism, Trump has suggested several times that the US could strike Iran after the November 3 US midterm elections .

He told the Right Side Broadcasting Network (RSBN) on Sunday that the war on Iran would end “very soon one way or the other”, adding that Tehran would either “make a deal, or we’ll just end it”.

articles.title: In 1981, Olivia Newton-John bought an Australian farm for $622,000; after planting 5,000 trees and creating wildlife habitat, she sold the 187-acre estate for $4.6 million as she invested more in cancer and wellness work
articles.summary: Olivia Newton-John’s Australian country estate was more than a celebrity home.
articles.body: Olivia Newton-John’s Australian country estate was more than a celebrity home. Over nearly four decades, the Grease star transformed the property into a landscape rich in trees, water features and wildlife before selling it in 2019 for $4.6 million. Reports by realestate dot com dot au, The Washington Post and Architectural Digest documented the estate’s natural surroundings, distinctive architecture and eventual sale, offering a glimpse into a quieter side of the singer’s life beyond her celebrated music career. Newton-John purchased the property at Dalwood, on the north coast of New South Wales, in 1981 for $622,000. Additional parcels of land were acquired over the following decades, bringing the estate to approximately 187 acres. The property was eventually listed for sale in 2019, after she had owned it for almost 38 years.A private retreat shaped by natureThe estate combined a French-inspired country residence with expansive grounds, established rainforest and several natural features. The main house was rebuilt in 2002, bringing together rustic interiors, stone arches, timber details and a spacious country-style kitchen. A separate guest accommodation offered additional living space.Outside, the property included two dams, a pond, a creek, a natural waterfall and a tennis court. Its proximity to Victoria Park Nature Reserve added to its appeal, with the surrounding landscape providing habitat for birds and other wildlife.Newton-John also invested in the land itself. Property reports credit her with planting around 5,000 trees and developing wildlife habitat during her ownership. The Washington Post, however, described the wider estate as having more than 10,000 trees, many planted over the years. The difference in reported figures suggests that the coverage may have counted the property's overall tree population rather than only those planted by the singer.The estate reflected an interest in the natural world that extended beyond landscaping. Newton-John had also co-founded Gaia Retreat & Spa in the Byron Bay hinterland in 2005, establishing a wellness destination focused on rest, relaxation and holistic experiences. The retreat remained part of her wider connection to the region even after the Dalwood property changed hands.The sale came during a shift towards cancer and wellness workIn 2017, Newton-John publicly disclosed that her breast cancer had returned and spread to her lower back. Two years later, she placed the Australian estate on the market as part of a wider period of property sales. Reporting by realestate.com.au and Domain subsequently linked the disposal of much of her real estate portfolio to her desire to invest further in her foundation and wellness work.Her work in this area included advocacy for cancer research and support for the Olivia Newton-John Cancer Wellness and Research Centre in Melbourne. She also remained closely associated with Gaia, which she helped establish to provide a restorative environment for guests.The Dalwood estate sold in July 2019 for $4.6 million, according to property reports published the following month. The buyer was identified as Carol Klinkert, whose husband, Stephen Klinkert, had an extensive background in the insurance industry. The reported sale price fell short of the more than $5 million initially sought for the property.Newton-John's sale marked the end of almost four decades of ownership, during which the property evolved into a secluded rural retreat. While the estate's market value had increased substantially from its original purchase price, its legacy also lay in the landscape she helped cultivate.The singer, who died in August 2022 at the age of 73, became widely known for her music, film career and later cancer advocacy. Her former Australian farm brought these different chapters into focus: a private sanctuary shaped by nature, a long-standing connection to the Byron Bay region and a property sold during her continued commitment to health and wellness initiatives.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Poland's constitutional crisis deepens as Prime Minister Tusk faces accusations of power grab
articles.summary: President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around as Poland's Constitutional Tribunal standoff triggered ambassador resignations and clashes.
articles.body: Friday’s late-night confrontation at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, which drew riot police and protesters and prompted President Karol Nawrocki to turn his plane around and return to Warsaw, has reignited a bitter debate over whether Prime Minister Donald Tusk is restoring the rule of law or overstepping constitutional limits. The dispute erupted after the tribunal announced the suspension of its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, a move that supporters of Tusk’s government described as necessary to restore judicial independence, while critics denounced it as an unconstitutional power grab. Marcin Przydacz, the head of the International Policy Bureau in Nawrocki’s office, took to European TV Monday morning denouncing Tusk’s actions, saying, "Even lawyers who are close to the Tusk government say that there's absolutely no legal basis for such behavior." POLISH PRESIDENT TURNS PLANE AROUND AFTER 'COUP' AT NATION’S TOP COURT The dispute is also triggering diplomatic fallout, with at least three Polish ambassadors resigning in protest. Przydacz, a former parliament member of the now-opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, says Poland’s permanent representative to the U.N. since 2021, Krzysztof Szczerski, resigned Monday, which followed the resignations over the weekend of the ambassadors to China and Romania. "This crisis didn’t begin on Friday," said Simone Rodan‑Benzaquen, senior envoy to Europe at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies. "Poland has been living with a deeply compromised Constitutional Tribunal for more than a decade." Rodan-Benzaquen said the confrontation cannot be understood in isolation. Parliament has continued appointing judges under Poland's constitution, but several of those appointments have been blocked from taking office amid a years-long standoff between the government, the presidency and the tribunal itself. "This isn't simply a case of Tusk deciding to pack a functioning, independent court ahead of an election," Rodan-Benzaquen tells Fox News Digital. "There is a genuine institutional crisis that predates his government, and a legitimate question of how to resolve it." That underlying conflict exploded into public view Friday after Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska suspended Święczkowski and his deputy, triggering protests outside the tribunal and prompting Nawrocki to abandon a trip to Senegal. Police detained three people after some demonstrators clashed with officers outside the court complex. HUNGARY AND POLAND DEFEND TOUGH MIGRATION POLICIES AS FRANCE REELS FROM VIOLENT UNREST Rodan-Benzaquen cautioned that concerns about Friday's actions are not limited to supporters of the opposition, saying they "raise serious questions about the legality and proportionality of the methods being used." Critics of the government have described Friday's events as an unprecedented assault on Poland's constitutional order. "My former boss, Margaret Thatcher, would have been absolutely appalled by what we're witnessing in Poland," Nile Gardner, director of the Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom at the Heritage Foundation told Fox News Digital. "This is clearly a crisis for Poland and an attempted coup by Donald Tusk." "This has all the hallmarks of a Soviet-style coup operation," added Gardner, who said Tusk waited until Nawrocki was traveling out of the country, accusing the prime minister of undermining the tribunal and further destabilizing Poland ahead of next year's election. "It's the sort of thing you'd expect actually from a third world dictator." Others reject the coup characterization. Boštjan Udovič, chair of international relations at the University of Ljubljana, says the dispute centers on the government's attempt to restore judicial arrangements that critics of the previous PiS government say were inconsistent with both Poland's constitution and European legal standards. "Tusk wants to restore the situation as required by the constitution and the international institutions," Udovič said. "I think that he hoped the transition would be easier." Tusk defended his government's actions as part of an effort to restore the rule of law, accusing both the president and the tribunal of improperly blocking judges elected by parliament from taking office. "The solution to the conflict is simple," he said on Monday. "The president recognizes the judges legally elected by [parliament], because that is what the Constitution stipulates." He accused Nawrocki of "choosing forceful confrontation, which could cost Poland very dearly. A democratic state under the rule of law cannot yield to violence." POLAND ARRESTS RUSSIAN ALLEGEDLY HIRED TO KILL UKRAINIAN-AMERICAN WHO WAS 'INCONVENIENT TO THE PUTIN REGIME' "Restoring the rule of law is essential," Rodan-Benzaquen says, warning against viewing the dispute purely through a partisan lens. "But the legitimacy of that restoration depends not only on its objectives, but also on the legality of the means used to achieve it." The divide in Poland has increasingly been reflected abroad, with European institutions and political leaders offering sharply different interpretations of the crisis. The European Commission has largely backed the Polish parliament's authority to appoint judges. European Commissioner Michael McGrath said selecting new judges lies within the powers of Poland's parliament. French opposition leader Marine Le Pen, meanwhile, accused Brussels of applying a double standard. "One cannot claim to defend democracy and the rule of law while remaining silent when the constitutional balance of a member state is gravely threatened," she posted on X. "The proliferation of such strong-arm tactics within the European Union itself is beginning to raise serious questions." "America is on Poland’s side," U.S. Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose posted to X, urging restraint. "Our concern is for the stability, security, and democratic future of a country we are proud to call our friend and ally… Poland has come too far and accomplished too much to let political differences, no matter how strongly felt, put any of that at risk." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP For Rodan-Benzaquen, the larger issue extends far beyond the events of Friday night. "One side claims to be defending constitutional order against the abuses of the other, while the institutions that should arbitrate the dispute have themselves become the object of the dispute," she said. With parliamentary elections in Poland only a year away, the battle over who gets to define the rule of law may prove more consequential than the confrontation that unfolded this weekend. Calling Tusk’s tactics "straight out of the Putin playbook," Gardner warns Poland is in "an incredibly dangerous situation right now, and the blame is squarely at the door of Donald Tusk and his government." The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: An Atlanta landlord started a $50,000 fundraiser to help families facing eviction during the pandemic; six years later, it has grown into a $16.5 million relief effort that has helped more than 5,500 families stay housed
articles.summary: What began as a small $50,000 fundraising campaign to help tenants struggling to pay rent during the 2020 coronavirus pandemic has grown into a $16.5
articles.body: What began as a small $50,000 fundraising campaign to help tenants struggling to pay rent during the 2020 coronavirus pandemic has grown into a $16.5 million housing support programme across the Atlanta metropolitan area. Jason Dozier, an Atlanta landlord and community advocate, started the emergency rent assistance campaign after seeing tenants in his own properties and nearby neighbourhoods lose their jobs during the early pandemic lockdowns. Six years later, the project has grown into a full housing non-profit organisation. It has distributed millions of dollars to help more than 5,500 families stay in their homes. According to figures published by the Good News Network, the programme has prevented thousands of formal eviction cases by providing emergency rent payments directly to property owners on behalf of tenants who have fallen behind.Origins of the emergency relief campaignThe project started in early 2020 when Dozier realised that federal emergency support money could take months to reach low-income workers who were at immediate risk of losing their homes. Instead of sending eviction notices to tenants who could not pay their rent, Dozier launched an online fundraising campaign. His goal was to raise $50,000 to cover overdue rent for struggling families in neighbourhoods across south Atlanta. "I saw neighbours losing their jobs overnight, and I knew that once an eviction notice is filed, it creates a permanent mark on a family's record that makes finding future housing almost impossible," Dozier stated in reporting published by the Good News Network. "We needed a fast, low-barrier way to bridge the gap before people ended up on the street." The campaign reached its fundraising target within a few weeks. It received small donations from local residents, neighbourhood groups, and community leaders. The quick response showed how much people needed fast financial help before their housing problems reached the courts.Scaling operations into a permanent non-profitDozier and local housing organisers soon realised that short-term financial help alone would not solve the larger problem of housing insecurity. They decided to turn the community campaign into a permanent non-profit organisation called the Housing Stability Fund. The organisation began working with local community foundations, charitable donors, and government agencies across Fulton and DeKalb counties to bring together funding. It also made the application process easier. Instead of requiring tenants to complete complicated paperwork, the organisation introduced simple income checks and direct payments to landlords. This helped reduce the time needed to process applications from several months to just a few days. According to operational records cited by the Good News Network, the non-profit raised and distributed more than $16.5 million in housing assistance between 2020 and 2026. The average grant provided to each family ranges from $2,500 to $3,500. The money covers unpaid rent and overdue utility bills, helping families keep both their homes and essential household services.Preventing eviction records and court backlogOne of the programme's main goals is to provide help before landlords file official eviction cases in magistrate court. Under Georgia law, an eviction filing becomes part of a tenant's public record, even if the person is never physically removed from the property. This can make it much harder for them to find another rental home in the future. The Housing Stability Fund works directly with landlords and tenants to reach agreements. These arrangements allow eviction proceedings to be put on hold while applications for financial assistance are reviewed. "Landlords generally do not want to evict tenants if there is a reliable way to get rent paid," Dozier explained in media interviews about how the programme works. "Eviction is expensive, time-consuming, and harmful for everyone involved. When we guarantee the payment, landlords choose stability over litigation." The organisation's work has also helped reduce pressure on magistrate courts across the Atlanta metropolitan area. These courts faced serious backlogs after federal eviction protection rules came to an end.Measuring long-term housing retentionFigures collected by the Housing Stability Fund show that direct financial assistance has helped many families remain in their homes over the long term. Follow-up surveys conducted by the organisation found that more than 85 per cent of families who received assistance were still living in stable housing twelve months after receiving emergency funding. Most families used the one-time payments to get through temporary financial problems, such as medical emergencies, seasonal job losses, or vehicle breakdowns. The organisation also provides support beyond financial grants. It connects participating families with local job training programmes, financial advice services, and legal support networks. These services are designed to help families improve their financial situation and remain housed in the future. The Atlanta programme has also attracted interest from housing advocates in other major US cities. They are looking at how similar partnerships between private organisations and public agencies could help reduce homelessness in urban areas. The Housing Stability Fund continues to provide daily emergency rental assistance across metropolitan Atlanta. articles.title: HRW calls on Zambia to halt post-election crackdown
articles.summary: Opposition figures arrested and disappeared since President Hakainde Hichilema claimed August victory.
articles.body:
Human Rights Watch (HRW) has called on Zambia’s authorities to halt the vicious clampdown on the political opposition that was launched following President Hakainde Hichilema’s victory in disputed elections in August.

The rights group demanded in a report released on Sunday that the authorities put a stop to the intensifying crackdown.

It accused Zambia’s government of silencing government critics, with several members of the opposition, as well as journalists and lawyers, arrested and some having disappeared in recent months.

“The post-election climate of intimidation, harassment, and repression has had a chilling effect on civic and political organizations, particularly on dissenting voices,” HRW said.

The group said that Zambian police and military “forcibly disappeared, arbitrarily detained, beat, and threatened opposition members and supporters as well as lawyers, journalists, and government critics in the days before and after general elections in August 2026”.

“Zambia’s government should break this dangerous cycle of repression,” added Ashwanee Budoo-Scholtz, deputy Africa director at HRW.

“The authorities should immediately halt the ongoing post-election crackdown, allow access to lawyers and provide medical care for those in detention, release everyone arbitrarily detained, and ensure accountability for abuses by security forces.”

Hichilema was sworn in for a second term as Zambia’s president following his victory in August. Critics have insisted that the election was marred by vote rigging.

As he was inaugurated at the National Heroes Stadium in the Zambian capital, Lusaka, his main rival Brian Mundubile was in detention , accused of treason after claiming the opposition had won the election.

Police raided Mundubile’s home the day after the August 13 elections. A former cabinet member, Mutotwe Kafwaya, was shot and killed during the operation.

HRW called on the Zambian authorities to institute an independent, impartial and thorough investigation into the matter.

About a dozen other opposition figures who have questioned the election results have been arrested.

Meanwhile, authorities suddenly closed the country’s courts two weeks after the election, a move that Zambian police stated was an “intelligence-led and preventive measure”, without providing details.

HRW noted that the closure prevents the opposition from filing legal challenges against the vote.

articles.title: Two boys arrested after Chandler's Ford Halloween party stabbings
articles.summary: Two teenage boys, both from Southampton, have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder.
articles.body:
Two teenage boys have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after five teenagers were stabbed at a Halloween party.

Officers said they were called shortly after 22:30 GMT on Saturday to Park Road in Chandler's Ford, Hampshire , where an "unknown group" had gained entry to the event.

Police said two boys remain in hospital having suffered serious injuries, with one 17-year-old victim in a life-threatening condition. The others have been discharged from hospital.

A 17-year-old and 16-year-old, both from Southampton, have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and remain in police custody.

Two witnesses told the BBC a fight started after a group came in over a garden fence, although they said the motive for the stabbings was unclear.

One of the teenagers said: "I was [standing] in the hallway near the exit and I saw someone I know pull up their shirt and say 'I've been stabbed'.

"And then I later saw him lying outside the front of the house with someone compressing his wound."

Police cordoned off parts of Park Road and the adjoining Valley Road.

Det Ch Insp Elizabeth Pirie said: "Whilst the two arrests are a significant development in our investigation, which has moved at pace since the incident was first reported to us, we still urge our communities to contact us with any information, no matter how small it may seem."

She added: "If you were at the party and have not spoken with officers yet, or you have any CCTV, mobile phone, dash cam or doorbell camera footage covering Park Road and the surrounding area, then please get in touch."

The force said throughout the coming week, local officers from the Neighbourhood Policing Team are visiting local schools and colleges to offer further advice and reassurance, as well as to support those directly and indirectly affected by this incident.

The vicar of Chandler's Ford, the Reverend Duncan Hollands, said: "It's awful, it's shocking, it's sad. Chandler's Ford is a very peaceful place. These sorts of things don't happen."

He said churches had opened their doors for people to pause for reflection or seek support.

St Boniface Church in Hursley Road will be open 09:00-17:00 through the week, while St Martin in the Wood in Queen's Road will be available Monday and Wednesday between 15:00 and 17:00.

articles.title: Jet may have experienced ‘some breakup’ before it crashed in Florida, killing 9, NTSB says
articles.summary: Officials said there may have been “some breakup” of the Learjet 60 before it crashed Sunday afternoon in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board.
articles.body: Officials said there may have been “some breakup” of the Learjet 60 before it crashed Sunday afternoon in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board. Among those killed in the crash where two children, ages 4 and 2, and their parents, the families of the victims said in a joint statement Monday. For Adam Robinson and Helen Sharp, their children Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were “the light of their lives,” the families said. The aircraft had departed from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera, Bahamas, the National Transportation Safety Board said at a news conference Monday. The plane crashed around 12:50 p.m. Sunday near the residential neighborhood of Cresthaven in Greenacres, about 7 miles southwest of West Palm Beach. The cause remains under investigation. “We do have some evidence that there was some breakup of the aircraft before impact. We’re still seeking to determine that,” NTSB member Tom Chapman said. Video of the crash captured on a car’s dashcam showed the jet plummeting into the road at a high speed, causing a fiery explosion. The crash left a large hole in the ground. Seven passengers and two crew members were on the jet. The passengers were identified Monday by their families as Adam Robinson and Helen Sharp and their children Emma and Charlie, as well as Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr, and Anita Maria Cetina. Reed and Fehr “were full of joy and adventure,” they said. Cetina cared for Emma and Charlie and “was truly part of the family,” they said. “She showed us a legacy of unconditional love and devotion,” the families said. The co-pilot was identified by her family as Nathalia Filgueiras, 20. Her sister Giulia Filgueiras said Nathalia learned to fly from her father, who is a pilot. “Flying was her biggest passion,” Giulia Filgueiras said. “That was her dream to become a pilot since she was very young.” In distressing air traffic control audio, a woman onboard the plane is heard saying, “Mayday, mayday. We’re descending 10,000 feet per minute.” She later yells and says the jet was descending at 20,000 feet per minute. “We’re gonna crash into the ground 722 Bravo Delta,” she screamed. About two minutes before the audio, the woman reported “light, clear ice” but said it was “manageable” and described “moderate turbulence.” She later said, “We’re picking up precipitation,” and asked to climb in altitude. Chapman said the request to climb was approved by air traffic control. “Less than 30 seconds later, a transmission from the airplane announced a descent, followed by a mayday call,” he said at the news conference. “About 12:48 Eastern, the airplane transmitted, ‘We are in an over-speed condition, descending,’ with the rest unintelligible. Subsequent communications described that the airplane was descending rapidly and gave an altitude callout. Sadly, all aboard were lost.” There was a flood watch in effect Sunday for southern Florida with numerous showers and scattered thunderstorms forecast to continue through Monday, according to the National Weather Service. The NTSB said weather conditions will be a major focus of the investigation. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said the jet “looked like a missile going down” because of its speed. He called the crash “cataclysmic.” He said the amount of debris spanned a “pretty significant distance.” Joel Flores, commissioner for Palm Beach County’s 3rd District, previously said that about 600 people were displaced from their homes after the crash. He said at a news conference on Monday that about 77 mobile homes near the wreckage site were among the homes evacuated and that it’s unclear when residents will be allowed to return home. Officials said they are working to re-establish access to the neighborhood. “Our concern right now on the county is obviously clearing the scene so that our residents can get back to normal,” Flores said. Learjet manufacturer Bombardier said the company was “deeply saddened” by the crash. “We cannot comment on the potential cause of this accident until the investigation is complete and we will fully support the investigating authorities and cooperate as needed,” Bombardier said.

articles.title: The 37 best cooking gifts, according to someone who tests and writes about kitchen gadgets all year
articles.summary: I found the best gifts for people who love to cook, including cookware, gadgets, and edible gifts from an array of brands, even favorites, like Le Creuset, Williams Sonoma, Staub and more.
articles.body: One of the best parts about the holidays is the abundance of homemade meals. If you come from a family that likes to cook, then you know how many reliable kitchen tools, gadgets and accessories it takes to host a great family dinner. You likely also know that finding the best cooking gifts to surprise your loved ones is a great way to show them how much you appreciate their passion. I’ve grown up in the kitchen, cooking and baking for decades, and I’ve worked for years as a food editor at multiple well-known food magazines, so I love selecting the perfect cooking gifts for people of all levels and backgrounds. Below, I rounded up some of the best cooking gifts to consider this year, including luxe appliances, indestructible cookware, useful gadgets, quirky accessories and more. I included popular bestselling items from my favorite brands and retailers, like Williams Sonoma, Le Creuset and of course, Amazon. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best cooking gifts in 2026 All of the cooking gifts below are either based on NBC Selected previous coverage and testing, and/or are from brands that are highly rated and have bestselling items with thousands of reviews on its site or Amazon. Best cookware and appliances Le Creuset’s Dutch oven is one of the brand’s most popular cookware items — and an NBC Selected favorite, so there was no way to create a gift guide for cooks without including it. It’s available in several colors, sizes, limited editions and is practically indestructible. The pot is made from enamel-coated cast iron and is safe on every cooking appliance. I’ve loved everything I’ve owned from Le Creuset because the pieces remain in great shape and last for years without scratches. It’s the perfect thing to splurge on if the home cook in your life is really special to you. GreenPan makes some of the best nonstick cookware available, particularly when it comes to PFAS-free options. I first got a complimentary cookware set for testing from the brand more than three years ago and I still use the pans today because they aren’t chipped or scratched. Plus, they’re dishwasher and oven safe, and they’re easy to wash by hand — I don’t have to do a ton of scrubbing to get them clean. A dishwasher safe food chopper is the ultimate affordable cooking gift because it reduces prep time so much. Your giftee will appreciate this gadget because it takes the trickiness out of chopping carrots, bell peppers, lettuce and onions (meaning no tears). It comes with multiple blade types that will allow them to mince or dice anything in any size. It also includes attachments for shredding (like cheese and zucchini) and slicing into rounds, for homemade potato chips. AeroGarden is one of our favorite brands here at NBC Selected because it sells products that make growing herbs easy, and helps us save money on fresh herbs that spoil before we’ve had a chance to use them. This hydroponic gardening system grows herbs five times faster than in soil, according to the brand, and since it grows indoors, you don’t have to worry about it getting the perfect amount of sunlight. The grow light has an adjustable height and helps to produce basil, mint, parsley and more. The brand’s popular olive oil, which is made and bottled in Spain, is some of the best I’ve ever used and tasted. It has a high smoke point and prevents me from accidentally burning food. Plus, I love that it comes in a high-quality squeeze bottle that doesn’t easily get misshapen. Maldon (pronounced mal-din), is a coarse sea salt that’s been harvested in England since 1882. It’s very different from table salt because it has a crunchy texture and each flake gives things like meat a pop of flavor, so you only need a small amount to give food the right amount of saltiness. This gift pairs well with Le Creuset’s salt cellar (see below). In her roundup of different types of salt, NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin says she puts Maldon on a lot of things she bakes and buys it in small buckets. I first tried this ultra-popular Williams Sonoma Peppermint Bark last December because I wanted to compare it to more affordable options I’ve tried. With that said, this bark is worth all of the hype it gets — it’s made with high-quality white and milk chocolate covered in pieces of crushed peppermint candy. It also has a substantial bite to it, so it’s nothing like a candy bar from the grocery store. The bark comes in a festive tin which makes it even easier to give as a gift to someone. Williams Sonoma also makes a peppermint bark-flavored coffee syrup for that home cook that’s also a coffee lover and takes jazzing up their cup of joe very seriously. If you’ve ever heard Ina Garten use the term “good vanilla,” this is exactly what she’s talking about. Vanilla bean paste is one of the most flavorful forms of vanilla you can use in baking, and it’s much more powerful and rich than traditional extract. This paste from Neilsen-Massey, which uses vanilla bean pods from Madagascar, has a thick syrup-like texture and it’s filled with small bits of fresh vanilla throughout. "There are multiple fatalities and casualties confirmed," the sheriff's office said. articles.title: Chance the Rapper’s foundation commits $500,000 to five Chicago high schools for career training as the New Chance Fund’s wider programme reaches more than 27,000 students
articles.summary: Chance the Rapper’s New Chance Fund has committed $500,000 to career-connected learning at five Chicago high schools, giving each campus $100,000 to spend
articles.body: Chance the Rapper’s New Chance Fund has committed $500,000 to career-connected learning at five Chicago high schools, giving each campus $100,000 to spend over three years. The grants flow through SocialWorks, his nonprofit organisation, in partnership with the philanthropic arm of Chicago Public Schools, and target skills such as barbering, culinary arts, carpentry and digital media. Since launching in 2017, the wider programme has supported 55 schools and reached more than 27,000 students, funding everything from arts spaces and computer science to educational travel. The fourth round turns the focus to practical, industry-aligned pathways from the classroom into real careers.Chance the Rapper surprises barbering and cosmetology students at Simeon Career AcademyThe announcement came in 2025, at Simeon Career Academy, where Chance the Rapper made a surprise visit to students in the school’s summer barbering and cosmetology programme, according to SocialWorks. A product of Chicago’s public schools and an alumnus of Jones College Prep, he chose a neighbourhood high school for the occasion. He aimed to encourage young people curious about the skilled trades. His second studio album, Star Line, had been released on 15 August.CBS News Chicago reported that the rapper took the auditorium stage to thunderous applause. He had come not to promote his new record but to present a cheque through his charity. Students in the barbering course told the broadcaster they enjoy the work, with one describing it as an art form and another praising a room where nobody is judged, and everyone is there to improve. Many hope to open their own shops one day.How five Chicago high schools will spend $100,000 each on equipment, internships and industry linksEach school drew up its own spending plan, covering everything from classroom equipment and industry-aligned field trips to internships, guest speakers and skill-building workshops. The shared goal is to build stronger bridges between lessons and the world of work.Dunbar Vocational Career Academy will direct its share towards equipment and resources for architecture, automotive body repair, broadcasting, cosmetology, culinary arts and health science, alongside industry partnerships and career events. Dyett High School for the Arts will widen postsecondary exposure for students and upgrade its digital media lab and its recording and podcast studio. Manley Career Academy will invest in equipment, supplies, field trips and hands-on training for culinary arts students.Prosser Career Academy plans to expand internships and career exploration for carpentry students and others in career and technical education, develop an integrated curriculum and help students earn industry-recognised certifications. At Simeon, the money will buy new styling chairs, upgraded workstations and other essential materials for the barbering and cosmetology programmes.From arts and computer science to travel, what the New Chance Fund has delivered since 2017The fund has changed its theme with every round. The first cohort concentrated on the arts and wider access to creative expression. The second backed computer science, building schools’ capacity for digital initiatives. The third paired advanced literacy with cultural immersion through travel, including college tours and field trips. Career-connected learning is the focus of the fourth.SocialWorks said the grants, supported by the charity and a network of philanthropic partners, have created 30 new or renovated career-connected learning and arts spaces. They have also brought in programming from more than 40 community organisations and sent nearly 300 students on out-of-state educational trips. Its count covers 51 recipient schools and more than $5.1 million in investment.Chicago Public Schools gave a slightly higher tally in a letter to staff and families the following day. It counted 55 schools, more than $5.2 million and 39 renovated or outfitted learning spaces.Why Chance the Rapper says career pathways and community giving matter for Chicago’s young peopleChance the Rapper said in the announcement that creating positive change in children’s lives “is our duty”, adding that it does not happen passively. He said the fund’s continued work helps students shape their own futures by finding real routes from the classroom into meaningful careers.Macquline King, who leads Chicago Public Schools, said the funding does more than pay for equipment. In her view, it nurtures confidence and creativity and lets students picture themselves in the careers they want, with the tools to get there. Justin Cunningham, co-executive director of SocialWorks, said the partnership shows what is possible when community and philanthropy unite, and he invited other supporters to help open more pathways.Chance the Rapper told CBS News Chicago it is “important for everybody to give back”, whoever they are and wherever they come from.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'The View' host Sara Haines lauds Haley Stevens' 'brave' endorsement of Mike Rogers
articles.summary: Sara Haines called Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens' cross-party endorsement of Mike Rogers "brave," pushing back on those who labeled the move as a betrayal.
articles.body: "The View" co-host Sara Haines defended Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., during a discussion on Monday about the Democrat's decision to endorse Michigan Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers over Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed, pushing back against critics who called the endorsement a betrayal. Co-hosts Sunny Hostin and Ana Navarro both argued that Stevens endorsed Rogers for the wrong reasons, with Hostin saying, "Shame on her," if the move was motivated by a bruised ego. Stevens said during an interview on Sunday that it was El-Sayed's "anger" and "lack of kindness" that led her to endorse Rogers. "I disagree. And I actually think that, although there’s a lot of Islamophobia here that are muddying the waters, there are deep concerns about his beliefs," Haines said. "Campaigning with Hasan Piker, you could not put enough room between me and that man. And we went after the Republicans for going around with Nick Fuentes, also problematic." "We have got to know when we denounce someone," she continued. "And if crossing party lines can be an act of conscience for Liz Cheney, I don’t know why the automatic response was that this was betrayal somehow." EL SAYED'S LEFT-WING ALLIES ATTACK 'EVIL' STEVENS AFTER BOMBSHELL ROGERS ENDORSEMENT Haines, a registered independent, said Stevens' decision was "brave." "Integrity is not just backing your party when you support your party," the co-host added. "The real test is backing them when it costs you something. I keep hearing, 'Donald Trump is so dangerous,' and that is true, but that can’t end every conversation we have about what we’re willing to accept on our own sides." "Honestly, the hateful rhetoric and demeaning language, I don’t have to agree with a candidate on everything at all, and compromise is absolutely necessary, but you cannot loan your loyalty and support out to a party," Haines continued. "They must earn it every single time. And that’s why this was actually a very brave thing for her to do." FORMER RIVAL DODGES FULL-THROATED EL-SAYED ENDORSEMENT AFTER BITTER SENATE PRIMARY Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff told Fox News Digital in a statement, "Haines’s defense is hard to square with the facts. I was one of the early Democrats who said El-Sayed needed to put real distance between himself and Hasan Piker. And he did. He said Piker did not speak for his campaign, stopped campaigning with him, and reportedly even called him directly to say his rhetoric was hurting the campaign and counterproductive. That all happened well before Haley Stevens’s last-minute endorsement." "So Haines is using an issue El-Sayed already addressed to excuse this wild switch-up, while openly acknowledging the Islamophobia on the other side and then instantly brushing past it," he added. Shroff argued that Haines was treating hate from one side as disqualifying, but not the other, and said, "That is not principled, balanced, or reasonable. It is just a glaring double standard." Co-host Whoopi Goldberg brought up the timing of the endorsement as Haines argued that El-Sayed had also told Stevens he did not want her to campaign with him. Navarro reiterated that she believed Stevens' decision was motivated by El-Sayed's reluctance to have her at the event. HALEY STEVENS' FIANCE HAMMERS EL-SAYED, SAYS HE'LL VOTE FOR ROGERS Fellow co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin said that Stevens had raised "real issues" about antisemitism. Griffin also compared Stevens endorsing Rogers with Liz Cheney endorsing former Vice President Kamala Harris earlier in the segment. "We shouldn’t just praise independents when Liz Cheney breaks with Republicans, because she thinks that’s the principled position. If this woman feels this is the principled position for her, she has every right to do that," Griffin said. Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed and Rogers campaigns for comment but did not immediately receive a response. Shroff argued the Cheney comparison did not hold up, telling Fox News Digital, "Cheney crossed party lines because of Trump’s conduct and her stated concerns about democracy. Stevens, by contrast, says she is crossing party lines because she cannot tolerate hate, yet she is endorsing Mike Rogers in a race where anti-Muslim hate has been Rogers’s central campaign strategy." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Moreover, Haley still maintains that Republicans — folks like Mike Rogers — are allowing Trump to act as a ‘dictator.’ It just doesn’t add up any way you try," he said.

articles.title: Crashed Learjet’s 20-year-old co-pilot remembered for her early love of flying
articles.summary: BOCA RATON, Fla. — In a neighborhood of palm-tree-lined streets and houses with perfectly manicured lawns, friends and relatives of Nathalia Filgueiras arrived at her family home to mourn the 20-year-old co-pilot who a day ago plummeted to her death in Florida aboard a Learjet 60 jet alongside eight other victims.
articles.body: BOCA RATON, Fla. — In a neighborhood of palm-tree-lined streets and houses with perfectly manicured lawns, friends and relatives of Nathalia Filgueiras arrived at her family home to mourn the 20-year-old co-pilot who a day ago plummeted to her death in Florida aboard a Learjet 60 jet alongside eight other victims. Filgueiras’ mother, Camila Corteleti; her older sister, Giulia Filgueiras; her stepfather, Thiago Corteleti; and her younger sister all gathered in the dining room. With eyes swollen from crying, they wore black and white as they waited to hear from authorities about her remains. Nicole Tarantino, 21, stopped by Monday to pay her respects to the family after waking up that morning to the news that her friend died in the plane crash. She and Filgueiras had known each other since they were in elementary school. “She was a beautiful person inside and out,” Tarantino told NBC News. Heartbroken and in tears, she said her friend always knew she wanted to be a pilot. “When it came to picking colleges, she was looking at aviation schools,” Tarantino said. “She was dedicated. She was only 20 years old doing all of that, and she excelled at it.” Growing up in a Brazilian household in Boca Raton, Florida, Filgueiras was inspired by her father, Allan Filgueiras, who is also a pilot. He was the one who taught her how to fly planes before she went on to earn her pilot license while still in high school. Filgueiras got her license in 2023, when she was a 17-year-old senior at West Boca Raton Community High School. At the time, WPEC, a news station in South Florida, reported that the Palm Beach County School District paid for Filgueiras to get her private pilot license through the school’s aviation academy. “Flying was her biggest passion,” Giulia Filgueiras told NBC News about her younger sister. “That was her dream, to become a pilot, since she was very young.” Nathalia Filgueiras’ last words echoed through a distressing air traffic control call Sunday. “Mayday, mayday. We’re descending 10,000 feet per minute,” she alerted. “We’re gonna crash into the ground, 722 Bravo Delta,” she can be heard saying, followed by a scream. After learning of her death, Allan Filgueiras told NBC News that his daughter was a first officer, better known as the right-seat, second-in-command co-pilot who helps navigate and operate a flight alongside a captain. The passengers killed in the crash were identified by their families Monday as Adam Robinson and Helen Sharp and their children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2. The other passengers were Rachael Reed, Charmi Fehr and Anita Maria Cetina, the families said on Facebook. Investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board said at a news conference Monday that they are still working to determine what caused the plane to crash in a neighborhood in Palm Beach County. Tom Chapman, an NTSB member, said the Learjet 60 jet that Filgueiras was co-piloting left Texas around 10:30 a.m. ET en route to the Bahamas. At 12:47 p.m. ET, the plane reported experiencing moderate turbulence after encountering “clear ice” 35,000 feet in the air. The pilots sent a request to move to 37,000 feet, which was granted, Chapman said. Thirty seconds later, the plane began to descend until it crashed. At the news conference, NTSB investigators and local officials called on any witnesses who may have captured the crash on video to come forward and help with the investigation. Those close to Filgueiras are choosing to remember the young woman for her determination in chasing her dreams. “She was a light, and she did what she loved,” Tarantino said. Erika Angulo reported from Boca Raton, Florida, and Nicole Acevedo from New York City.
