articles.title: Allergies acting up? You may need a humidifier.
articles.summary: Find the best humidifiers to relieve allergies and dry skin. Shop humidifiers from brands like Honeywell, Levoit, Vicks and more.
articles.body: Those who live in dry or frigid climates know that a little humidity goes a long way for the skin. Humidifiers can help introduce more moisture into your home by emitting water vapor into the air, which helps alleviate dry skin, chapped lips, nosebleeds and other dry-weather conditions. “Dry skin can have an impaired barrier function, making it more prone to irritation and inflammation — humidifiers help prevent winter dermatitis,” says board-certified dermatologist Dr. Jessie Cheung. More moisture in the air also helps slow down the transmission of microbes in your home — which helps with allergies — and combats irritation of your skin, nasal passages, throat and more due to dry air, according to experts. (But keep in mind, humidifiers require weekly cleaning to avoid build up of mold and bacteria.) To help you find the best humidifier for your space, I spoke to experts about the benefits of humidifiers, the different types available and what to consider when shopping for one. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Top-rated humidifiers to shop All of the humidifiers below are either recommendations from our experts, NBC Selected staff favorites, or are top-rated options with at least a 4-star average rating from 100 or more reviews on Amazon. Every winter, I have so much trouble with the dry air and usually wake up with a painful, bloody nose. I also never had enough space for a humidifier in my tiny NYC apartment, so when I moved to a bigger place a few months ago, I was finally able to use this bedside Canopy one. It has made a huge difference when it comes to my quality of sleep and how comfortably I wake up. I also love how it looks; I have the sage green one and it’s the perfect look and size for my nightstand. NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman and her family love Canopy — both of her kids have a Nursery Humidifier 2.0 in their bedrooms, plus they use the Baby Bath Tub Filter. Recently, the brand sent her their new Canopy Portable Humidifier 2.0 and she decided to keep it for herself. “My skin gets incredibly dry in the winter, particularly the inside of my nose. I set this up at my desk to use while I’m working and love how small and easy to set up it is,” she says. “The best part is, I can easily transport it to my nightstand to use while I’m sleeping. The humidifier also has a dimmable nightlight, that is great for middle-of-the-night bathroom runs. After a few weeks of using it, I’ve noticed my skin is much less dry, too.” Levoit is one of our favorite humidifier brands, and NBC Selected special projects associate Vanessa Bethea swears by this model during allergy season, especially since her small apartment doesn’t have the best airflow. “I like that it’s a simple humidifier that I can keep by my bed and doesn’t require an app or remote. It’s also easy to refill from the top, has dishwasher-safe parts and is small enough to store away when I’m not using it,” she says. This cool mist, ultrasonic humidifier is designed to automatically shut off when the device detects it has run out of water. The essential oil tray also lets the machine double as a diffuser to add a pleasant scent throughout your home. Since it humidifies large spaces, you can use it in a bedroom or even the living room. It’s also slim and tall, which means it doesn’t take up too much surface area on a counter or side table. The Vicks Warm Mist Humidifier can temporarily relieve cold symptoms and congestion by pumping out a warm mist into the air, according to the brand. It comes with a large tank opening for easy filling and is designed for medium- to large-sized rooms. This humidifier’s lightweight design — slightly under 1.5 pounds — makes it ideal for tighter, cozier spaces, according to the brand, such as a small bedroom or home office. The top of the humidifier is also transparent, so you can always see the water level without worrying about it running out abruptly. It also includes a nightlight to help create a more soothing sleep environment, according to Pure Enrichment. If you’re looking for a cool-mist humidifier to put in your child’s room, this budget-friendly Vicks model might be a good option. It has an antimicrobial filter that removes impurities to prevent white dust in hard water areas, according to Cheung. The humidifier has a changing light, adjustable mist settings and a transparent top. Plus, “it has the bonus of a relaxing starry sky projector,” she says. This ultrasonic humidifier from Levoit includes dual-temperature control, which means you can set a cool or warm temperature. It also comes with a remote that lets you turn the humidifier on and off, as well as control mist levels. “It has a large tank and provides humidistats to avoid over-humidification,” says Cheung. The humidifier also has a transparent water tank and functions relatively quietly, according to the brand. Since it covers such large areas, you could use this one for your entire home or apartment. A favorite of NBC Selected editorial director Lauren Swanson, the Hey Dewy Facial Humidifier can help hydrate your face throughout the day. It’s both wireless and rechargeable, so you can travel with it. It also offers continuous and intermittent mist settings, as well as a soft LED light to keep next to your nightstand. This humidifier weighs 2.2 pounds, making it one of the most lightweight options on this list. It also comes with a personal steam inhaler for cough and cold that you can set up by replacing the humidifier tank with the included inhaler attachment, according to the brand. This model can heat water up to 131 degrees to produce a warm mist, according to the brand. Cheung says this warm-mist humidifier is especially quiet because it doesn’t have a fan — although users may hear the sound of bubbling water. “There’s also no costly filters to replace, but it’s important to clean the mineral scale from a warm-mist humidifier to keep it running,” she says. How to shop for a humidifier The best humidifier is the one that you will use and maintain regularly. Whether you’re looking for your first humidifier or want to upgrade your current model, our experts highlight the different types of humidifiers, along with several features to keep in mind below. Type of humidifier: Humidifiers come in two main types: cool-mist humidifiers (evaporative and ultrasonic) and warm-mist humidifiers (vaporizer). The one you choose depends on your own space and needs. For instance, warm-mist humidifier models are best if you live in a cold but very dry climate; a cool-mist humidifier is best for people who live in a warm but arid environment.Automatic shutoff: Self-regulating humidifiers can automatically turn off. This avoids putting too much moisture in the air, which can speed the growth of mold and mildew, says Cheung.Mold resistance: Any mold that forms within the water or machine can disperse into the air, so this feature helps keep the water clean. However, even with mold-resistant humidifiers, it is imperative to clean them at least once weekly to avoid buildup, our experts say.Tank size and speed settings: The size of the tank and the different speed settings can affect how long the humidifier can run before needing a refill, as well as the size of the room it can rehydrate. Portable units range in size from one liter to six gallons. A two-gallon humidifier will usually run for 12 or more hours on low, but a one-liter humidifier will require refilling every eight hours or so.Room size: The size of your humidifier largely depends on the size of your room, according to our experts. For smaller rooms under 400 square feet, a humidifier with up to 1.5 gallons is sufficient. For a medium room between 400 and 1,000 square feet, a tank size between one and three gallons is needed. A large room of over 1,000 square feet should have a humidifier with a tank size of more than three gallons.Multiple uses: In addition to adding moisture into the air, some humidifier models are also able to purify the air, diffuse essential oils through a separate chamber and work with a nebulizer attachment. What are the different types of humidifiers? Although there are two main types (warm and cold mist), there are multiple versions of the latter, according to our experts. Cool-mist humidifiers Cool-mist humidifiers help reintroduce moisture into your home by pumping a cool mist into the air. These humidifiers can be a bit noisier than warm-mist humidifiers as they typically contain a fan. There are two main types of cool-mist humidifiers: evaporative and ultrasonic. Evaporative humidifiers create a very fine mist that isn’t always visible to the human eye. Unlike warm-mist humidifiers, these humidifiers have no heating element, so there is no risk of burns, says Cheung. They work by using a fan to blow air through a filter. However, the fans can be noisy, and the filter should be cleaned regularly to prevent bacteria and mold from growing. Ultrasonic humidifiers use high-frequency sound vibrations outside the human hearing range to expel water droplets into the air as a cool mist. They usually have a small fan to disperse the mist over large areas. “These devices don’t use heat and are quiet, but do require maintenance to keep them free of mold and bacterial overgrowth,” says Cheung, adding that she prefers this type because it doesn’t have a filter that needs to be replaced. Warm-mist humidifiers Warm-mist humidifiers — also known as vaporizers — have an internal heater that boils the water before releasing it into the air as steam, creating a warm mist. They’re typically more affordable and quieter than cool-mist humidifiers, and they can slightly warm up the air in the wintertime. Our experts say users should avoid sitting too close to steam vaporizers and avoid putting them in children’s rooms since they can get very hot. How often should you clean your humidifier? You should clean your humidifier at least once a week if you use it regularly. Otherwise, clean it at least once a month. To clean it, unplug it, pour out any residual water, wipe away any grime with a paper towel and use a sprayable dish soap to coat the inside of the tank. Wipe the tank with a damp paper towel. You can also add equal parts white vinegar and water to the tank, let it sit for about half an hour, pour it out and then rinse with a damp paper towel and let it dry. articles.title: Bodies believed to be those of missing Missouri couple found on neighboring property
articles.summary: On November 1, bodies believed to be Leo and Katherine Lindeman were found on a property neighboring their Anderson, Missouri, home. They had been missing since around September 16.
articles.body: More than six weeks after Leo and Katherine Lindeman vanished from their Anderson, Missouri, home, two bodies believed to be those of the missing couple have been found on a neighboring property, according to a November 2 press release from the McDonald County Sheriff’s Office. A dog was found alive near the bodies, according to the release. The Lindemans’ small dog, Itty Bitty, went missing along with the couple in mid-September. Dateline featured the Lindemans’ story in its ‘Missing in America’ digital series last week. Investigators believe the couple vanished from their rural property around September 16. They were reported missing to the McDonald County Sheriff’s Office by a family friend on September 24, after they failed to show up for a planned weekly dinner. The Lindemans’ niece LaShawnda Lindeman told Dateline that on September 28, a private drone operator from Arkansas met up with the family at the property to help search for Leo and Katherine. The search at that time turned up nothing. On September 29, the McDonald County Sheriff’s Office searched the Lindemans’ 15-acre property but found no sign of the couple, according to LaShawnda. According to Monday’s press release, a property owner reported finding a body on November 1. When a McDonald County deputy arrived at the scene, the deputy discovered a second body in the area, along with a dog. “The bodies were located in a heavily wooded area adjacent to the property of a couple who had previously been reported missing from the Dogwood Drive area of Anderson,” the release stated. “Identification is expected to be made later this week, pending autopsy results and confirmation by the appropriate authorities.” LaShawnda says investigators told her they have not yet determined a cause or manner of death for either individual. The investigation remains ongoing. Dateline reached out to the McDonald County Sheriff’s Office for further information but has not yet received a response. Anyone with information regarding Leo and Katherine Lindeman’s case should call the McDonald County Dispatch Center at 417-223-4318. articles.title: US midterms 2026: What polls reveal about Democratic, Republican voters
articles.summary: From the economy and cost of living to immigration, polls suggest where American voters agree and disagree.
articles.body:
Americans will vote in the US midterm elections on Tuesday, with the economy, the cost of living, and immigration among the top issues. While Democrats and Republicans share concerns about the rising cost of living, recent surveys suggest differences in how they view the economy, President Donald Trump, and other key issues.

In an NBC poll released on Sunday, 75 percent of respondents said they were dissatisfied with the state of the US economy, and 51 percent said they were dissatisfied with their personal financial situation.

Other surveys conducted in October also offer a look into how voters from both parties felt about their finances and which issues mattered most.

What issues matter most to Democrats and Republicans?

The economy is the main concern for US voters, but Democrats and Republicans vary on the importance of issues like healthcare, immigration, and crime.

A Pew Research Centre survey, conducted between September 28 and October 4, suggested that 84 percent of registered voters considered the economy very important to their midterm vote. It was the top issue for 82 percent of respondents who prefer Republican candidates, and 88 percent for those who back Democrats.

However, the two groups differed on other issues.

About 85 percent of Democratic Party supporters considered the future of democracy very important, compared with 69 percent of Republicans. Healthcare was a priority for 82 percent of Democrats, compared with 53 percent of Republicans.

Republican supporters were more concerned about immigration, with 72 percent saying it was very important, compared with 53 percent of Democrats.

Violent crime was also more important to Republican supporters, at 64 percent, compared with 37 percent Democrats.

A KFF survey , conducted by the Kaiser Family Foundation, an independent nonprofit, from September 16 to 21, suggested 42 percent of registered voter respondents trusted Democrats more to handle healthcare costs, compared with 22 percent who trusted Republicans.

On the cost of living, 39 percent trusted Democrats more, while 25 percent preferred Republicans.

What grade do Democrats and Republicans give Trump’s second term?

Views of President Trump and his economic policies remain divided along party lines.

In the Pew Research Centre survey, 91 percent of Democratic respondents and those who leaned Democratic believed Trump’s economic policies had made things worse.

Among Republican supporters, 39 percent said his policies had improved the economy, 35 percent said they made conditions worse, and 25 percent said they had little effect.

In the November 1 NBC News poll, 40 percent of registered-voter respondents approved of Trump’s overall job performance, compared with 60 percent who disapproved.

How do Democrats and Republicans feel about the economy?

Americans are concerned about rising costs, but Democrats are more likely than Republicans to express negative feelings about economic conditions.

In an October Pew Research survey , 36 percent of Republicans rated the US economy as excellent or good, compared with just 9 percent of Democrats or Democrat-leaning voters.

However, the majority in both groups expressed concern about the cost of essential goods and services.

According to PEW, 82 percent of Democrats and Democratic leaners were concerned about food and consumer prices, compared with 62 percent of Republicans and Republican leaners.

Healthcare costs concerned 80 percent of Democrats and 57 percent of Republicans, while petrol and energy prices worried 81 percent of Democrats and 65 percent of Republicans.

A Fox News poll released on October 14 also had 74 percent of registered voter respondents rating the economy negatively, and 60 percent identified the cost of living as their biggest economic concern.

The November 1 NBC News poll found that 53 percent of Republican respondents were dissatisfied with the state of the economy.

The Pew Research Center also found that abortion and gun policy were less central to Democratic respondents in comparison with 2022. Among Republican voters, education policy and energy policy were less important than they were four years ago.

Are Americans satisfied with their financial situation?

In the NBC poll, 51 percent of registered voters were dissatisfied with their personal financial situation, compared with 49 percent who were satisfied.

It was the first time in 30 years of NBC polling that dissatisfaction with personal finances outweighed satisfaction.

In an NPR/PBS News/Marist poll on October 19-20, 38 percent of likely voters said their finances had gotten worse over the past year, 44 percent said they had remained about the same, and 15 percent said they had improved.

A total of 51 percent of Democratic likely voters said their finances had deteriorated, compared with 21 percent of Republicans.

In a Reuters/Ipsos survey conducted from September 30 to October 5, 71 percent of Democrats and 57 percent of Republicans said their incomes had not kept pace with rising prices.

Eric Ham, a former Democratic congressional staffer and Senate national security adviser, said that Trump’s global tariffs and the US-Israel war on Iran had added to the financial pressure on American households.

“Americans are paying more not just in terms of self-inflicted wounds that President Donald Trump implemented through tariffs, but also if you look at this war of choice,” Ham told Al Jazeera.

Are Democrats or Republicans more enthusiastic about voting?

Democratic voters reported higher enthusiasm about participating in the elections.

In the Marist poll, 91 percent of likely Democratic voters were enthusiastic or very enthusiastic, compared with 86 percent of Republicans and 76 percent of Independents.

John Fury, a former Republican congressional staffer, said the final days of campaigning were focused on turnout.

“This is not a persuasion election. This is a get-out-the base election,” Fury said.

In a KFF survey, Democratic candidate supporters were 25 percentage points more likely than Republican supporters to describe themselves as “more motivated” than usual to vote (63 percent versus 38 percent).

The November 1 NBC News poll also reported high interest in the elections, with 70 percent of registered voters rating their interest at nine or 10 on a 10-point scale.

Surveys conducted in the final weeks before the election suggested voters preferred Democratic candidates or Democratic control of Congress over Republicans.

An NBC poll conducted on October 28-30 and published on November 1 suggested that 52 percent of registered voters preferred Democratic control of Congress compared with 45 percent who preferred Republican control.

Similarly, the Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted from October 22 to October 26 suggested that 53 percent of likely voters would vote for or lean towards the Democratic candidates in their district, compared with 44 percent who supported Republicans.

These surveys measure voting sentiment, but they do not reflect the results of the individual races.
